question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Meta)

calls.reasoning: Meta guided Q3 2026 revenue to $61-64B (~1% FX headwind) after Q2 came in at $60.80B (+28%). In 2025 every quarter beat the top of the guide by $0.5-2.0B. Both 2026 quarters landed about $0.2B under the top. Consensus is ~$63.2B. A $64B result is ~25% YoY growth vs Q3'25 ~$51.24B, about Q2's constant-currency pace, so the median sits just under the top of the guide. Going above $67B would need a beat larger than any recent one (priced at 1%); going below $61B has no plausible mechanism. Market check: none found on Polymarket or Manifold. The saved Kalshi page lists Meta KPI markets but shows no revenue prices, and I couldn't reach bookmakers. Caveat: live web tools failed this run, so the evidence comes from earlier runs' saved dossiers (Oct 7, 2026) and isn't freshly verified.

calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on all facts: the $61-64B guide with ~1% FX headwind, Q2'26 at $60.80B (+28%), the 2026 pattern of landing ~$0.2B under the top, 2025 beats above the top, consensus ~$63.2B, and a Q3'25 base of ~$51.24B. The one factual dispute, the earnings date (Oct 28 vs Nov 4), doesn't change which report resolves the question (Q3 2026 is the first after September either way). The $10B legal accrual was confirmed by all runs to be an expense, so it doesn't affect revenue. The main judgment call is how much weight the 2026 near-top pattern gets versus the 2025 beat-the-top pattern. I weighted 2026 more (the recent guide regime), which gives a median of ~$63.8B, consistent with a two-year growth-stack cross-check. I widened the 10-90 slightly beyond the runs' ~$2.0-2.15B because FX moves since July and the stability of the guidance regime couldn't be verified without web access. I kept a 1% upper escape for a beat larger than any recent one, and declared no lower escape. No market anchor exists.
